summary: Direct extraction and inspection of the actual packaged NSIS installer, proving the runtime DLLs identified by this phase's audit genuinely ship inside it - not just staged in a build directory that never made it into the final artifact.
extractionMethod: 7z x "Church Intelligence Platform_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe" (p7zip-full installed this phase specifically to perform this verification)

installerNsiPlacementProof.conclusion: All three DLLs are placed directly into $INSTDIR (the same directory as cip-desktop.exe), the directory Windows' default DLL search order checks first - not a nested 'resources' subfolder that the loader would not find automatically. A matching Delete entry for each DLL is also present in the uninstaller section, so uninstall correctly removes them.

extractedInstallerContents: $PLUGINSDIR/System.dll (NSIS-internal, not part of the installed app)

extractedFileVerification.cip-desktop.exe: PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64 (stripped to external PDB), for MS Windows, 11 sections
extractedFileVerification.libstdc++-6.dll: PE32+ executable (DLL) (console) x86-64 (stripped to external PDB), for MS Windows, 11 sections
extractedFileVerification.libgcc_s_seh-1.dll: PE32+ executable (DLL) (console) x86-64 (stripped to external PDB), for MS Windows, 11 sections
extractedFileVerification.libwinpthread-1.dll: PE32+ executable (DLL) (console) x86-64 (stripped to external PDB), for MS Windows, 12 sections
extractedFileVerification.WebView2Loader.dll: PE32+ executable (DLL) (console) x86-64, for MS Windows, 9 sections

installerSizeChange.note: A real, substantial increase despite NSIS's LZMA compression, consistent with three additional real DLLs (4.86MB combined, post-strip) being bundled

automatedVerification: This entire extraction-and-check sequence is now the last step of scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh itself - the script fails loudly if any of the three DLLs is missing from the packaged installer, so this is not a one-off manual check but a build-time gate on every future run.
